text:
Cutter Gauthier is the reason anyone outside Orange County is watching the Ducks right now. He has 14 points in his last 10 games, and NHL.com ran the headline "Gauthier Continues to Make History" this week. The chances behind it (11.1 expected points over that stretch) say most of the heater is real, which is the best news Anaheim has had in a while.

The rest of the picture is harder. The Ducks are 12-14-1 and 3-7-0 in their last ten, with a goal difference of minus one that flatters a team getting 49% of the expected goals and only 46% at five on five. They have scored about 13 more goals than their chances deserve. That cushion is all that keeps them in range, because the goaltending is giving it straight back: Lukas Dostal has allowed 8.6 more goals than expected over his last five starts, Ville Husso 4.2 over his.

Leo Carlsson went on injured reserve with an upper-body injury, so the middle of the lineup thins out just as Beckett Sennecke returns to the top line and top power play beside Gauthier and Mikael Granlund. That line scores (7 goals for, 5 against) but bleeds chances the other way.

Our numbers give Anaheim a 35% shot at the playoffs. What we'd watch: whether either goalie steadies before Gauthier cools off, because one of those two things is probably coming.
